content:
maya: Quick async standup for API gateway + routing policies + auth + rate limits. Drop 1) what you did yesterday 2) blockers 3) plan for today. I’ll start.

liam: 1) landed the new route priority selector for canary traffic, pushed to staging. 2) blocker: noticed increased 429s for a specific client when bursty traffic hits the same shard. 3) today: investigate burst handling (token bucket params) and tune shard routing.

sasha: 1) finished the auth middleware change to surface client_id in headers for downstream services. Deployed to staging. 2) blocker: intermittent refresh_token failures on /v1/stream routes — reproduces when sequence > 4096 tokens. Logs show 401 from auth service. 3) today: run deeper trace with xsrf headers and add extra logging around token refresh path.

jordan: 1) reviewed liam’s routing unit tests and left comments. 2) blocker: holding on merging because we need a docs blurb for ops about new priority behavior. 3) today: write the short ops README and unblock the merge. Ping @alex for a quick doc read.

alex: 1) FYI I’m OOO half day this morning but glanced at the PR. 2) blocker: need a clear rollback path if priority selector misroutes traffic — can we keep old behavior behind a feature flag? 3) today: push a small change to make selector opt-in via feature flag and add a fallback to round-robin.

liam: quick note — the 429 spike correlates with client X sending many small concurrent requests. I think batching/kqueueing on client side would help, but we should adjust server-side smoothing. Sending a small patch to change token_bucket: refill_interval from 100ms -> 50ms for staging.

deploy-bot: canary-deploy:api-gateway-priority-selector started by liam at 1825032250 — 10% traffic to canary nodes. Monitoring: latency, error-rate, rate-limit-violations.

sasha: added a debug config snippet to staging if we need to reproduce the token refresh path faster:
```yaml
auth_middleware:
  debug_refresh: true
  log_level: debug
  token_refresh_threshold: 30s
```
placing this behind a short-lived flag.

jordan: @maya once alex merges the feature-flag change i’ll update the ops README and send an alert channel note before promoting canary -> 50%.

maya: thanks — couple of asks: 1) liam/sasha pair on the 429/auth refresh link — if you can validate with the debug flag that’d be great. 2) alex please make the flag default-off and wire a quick metric that shows route-fallbacks when enabled. 3) jordan add the rollback steps at top of the ops README (how to flip feature flag and revert canary).

alex: ack, will add metric and make default-off. plan to have the tiny flag PR up by lunch.

liam: if we see more 429s after the refill change, i’ll throttle canary down and open a quick incident-runbook draft.

deploy-bot: canary-deploy:api-gateway-priority-selector at 50% traffic started at 1825032390 by jordan — rolling window check: 5m.

sasha: quick debugging note — found one client that uses an outdated SDK which batches very short bursts; filed a support ticket to ask them to upgrade. That may reduce load spikes.

maya: perfect. keep this thread updated with any regressions. ping me if you need the hotline or org-wide incident. :+1:
